Quick quality control of the journals

Source: R/landmark_journal.R
landmark_journal_qc.Rd

Reports, for the LAST record of every key, what a coordinate table does not show: expected points never placed, points still at their seed (never checked), points snapped by a convention (adjusted: 3 or 4 brought back to the maximum body depth), points declared non-measurable, and whether the scale is known. Sorted worst first.

Usage

landmark_journal_qc(journal_dir, expect = c(1:19, 23L))

Arguments

journal_dir

Journal directory, or a journal already read with landmark_journal_read().

expect

Points a complete specimen must carry. Defaults to the 19 FISHMORPH landmarks and the derived head-base point 23; for the FISHMORPH reference target, whose records always carry the axis point 22, use c(1:19, 22, 23).

Value

A data.frame, one row per key: row_key, specimen, species, photo_file, timestamp, n_missing/missing, n_seeded/seeded, n_adjusted/adjusted, n_na, has_scale.

See also

landmark_journal_status(), consolidate_landmarks()

Examples

d <- file.path(tempdir(), "journal_qc_demo")
jr <- landmark_journal_open(d, operator = "AT")
#> Session journal: /tmp/RtmpFjKqwk/journal_qc_demo/landmarks_AT_20261027T065930Z.tsv
landmark_journal_append(jr, "fish_01", cbind(c(10, 60), c(20, 22)), 1:2,
                        status = c("1" = "clicked", "2" = "seeded"))
landmark_journal_qc(d, expect = 1:3)
#>   row_key specimen species photo_file                timestamp n_missing
#> 1 fish_01                             2026-10-27T06:59:30.597Z         1
#>   missing n_seeded seeded n_adjusted adjusted n_na has_scale
#> 1       3        1      2          0             0     FALSE
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
